title: Parachute launch: Slim observability deck for Console GA
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We need a minimal, launchable observability surface for Console that gives engineers and platform owners quick answers about latency, errors, and cost during GA. Given scope and implementation velocity constraints, this ticket captures the scope reductions (parachute cuts) for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown so we can hit a stable, testable build by the GA freeze.

Goal: Deliver a focused set of Console observability features that provide actionable signal for debugging production regressions and understanding unit economics, while deferring lower-priority surfaces to post-GA.

Scope retained (MVP):
- Core Health Dashboard: 3 cards (request rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate) aggregated at the customer-account level with 14-day retention.
- Top-5 Routes view: list of routes by request volume with basic filters (time range, region). No per-token or per-model microbreakdown in MVP.
- Tracing (light): distributed trace sampling for latency spikes. UI shows top-level spans, span duration, and an error flag. No deep flamegraph UI or full-span inspector in MVP.
- Cost Overview: aggregated cost by model family and by account (daily rollup). Includes estimated $/k token and a chart for 30 days. No per-request token breakdown or token-level attribution in MVP.
- Alerts & Links: simple alert rule templates (latency, error-rate) and direct links from alert to the Top-5 Routes and Trace view.

Scope removed / deferred (cuts):
- Live tail / real-time streaming of traces (defer until post-GA).
- Per-token cost attribution and token-level trace correlation.
- Full span inspector (stack trace + headers) and trace flamegraph visualizations.
- Unlimited retention/advanced search (keep 14 days for GA; long-term retention is an add-on post-GA).
- Per-tenant fine-grained route cost breakdown beyond Top-5.
- Advanced sampling controls in UI (use backend defaults for GA).

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied for this ticket to be Done):
1) Core Health Dashboard is viewable in Console and shows correct p50/p95 latency and error rate for synthetic traffic (verify with load test ID: LT-2025-03-01).
2) Top-5 Routes view reflects route volume and filters functionally (time range, region). Cross-check counts against raw ingestion metrics (monitoring query: metrics.calc.route_counts).
3) Tracing light view surfaces sampled traces for latency spikes and flags error spans. Clicking a trace opens a summarized view (top-level spans + timestamps).
4) Cost Overview shows daily rollups by model family and account; numbers reconcile to billing export within 2% for the test window.
5) Alert templates can be attached to a project and the alert-to-dashboard links resolve to the correct Console views.
6) UI performance: pages must load within 2s for cached queries and within 4s for cold queries during standard QA cluster load.
7) Security/compliance: only users with the existing Console observability role can view dashboards; no additional PII surfaced in UI.
8) Documentation: PRD and ship notes updated with lists of deferred items and upgrade path to the full observability surface.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We prioritize fast time-to-insight for ops teams over deep forensic tools at GA. Deep inspection features add significant backend indexing and retention costs which would delay release.
- Aggregated cost by model-family gives product teams immediate unit economics visibility; token-level attribution is valuable but high-cost and lower priority for initial customers.

Implementation notes for Eng:
- Use existing metrics ingestion pipeline; add one rollup job for daily cost aggregation (ENG-8921).
- Tracing will reuse our sampling backend but limit UI payload size to the top-level spans only.
- Dashboard cards should be parameterizable by account id and region via query params to keep UIs lightweight.

QA plan and acceptance tests:
- Run synthetic traffic scenarios (LT-2025-03-01) to validate dashboards and cost reconciliation.
- Fault injection (partial region outage test) to validate graceful degradation and fallback links.
- Security check to confirm role-based access gating.

Rollout and rollout guardrails:
- Beta rollout to 5 pilot customers (support notified) with feature flag. Monitor error-rate and cost-reporting reconciliation for 72 hours before expanding.
- Telemetry events: dashboard.view, trace.open, cost.view; instrument counts and latency for each.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Retention: Can infra support 14-day retention without additional infra spend? (Asked to ENG infra owners 2025-02-14).
- Metric reconciliation tolerance: Is 2% acceptable for finance? Finance asked for 0.5% but we recommend 2% for GA (pending sign-off).

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (consolidated): https://confluence.redwood.ai/Console/Observability/PRD-slim-deck 
- Design mocks (MVP screens): https://drive.google.com/console-obsv/mvp-mocks 
- Implementation epic: ENG-8921 (rollups & tracing light)
- Load test: LT-2025-03-01 results: internal-dashboard/reports/LT-2025-03-01
- Example GH PR for dashboard card framework: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6123

Stakeholders and reviewers: Marco Ruiz (owner/assignee), Priya Nair (Design reviewer), Elias Thompson (SRE), Finance lead: Rowan Patel.

Follow-ups (post-GA backlog):
- Token-level cost attribution (post-GA Q2)
- Full trace inspector and flamegraphs (post-GA Q2)
- Retention tiers and long-term storage add-on pricing (post-GA commercialization)

Notes from review: Design signaled that condensed cards must be readable at 320px width; engineering flagged a potential 2-day delay if daily rollup runs conflict with billing export window. We should keep communication channel open with Finance to finalize reconciliation threshold.
